examples.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 1 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-\text{i})\cdot (1+2\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & (-\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot 2 \\ 1\cdot (1+2\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & 1\cdot (1-\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})+(-1) & (-1-\text{i})+2\text{i} \\ (1+2\text{i})+(-2) & (1-\text{i})+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -1+\text{i} \\ -1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}e & f \\ g & h\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 2-3\text{i} & 1-6\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 2-3\text{i} & 1-6\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=3,d=1,e=5$ and $h=-6.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=3\cdot 1+5\cdot (-6)=-27.
$$
